structure: Part 7 read the rest of the parties section and the contact section of the high-risk plants linear journey in repos/trade-imports-plants-frontend. Identification numbers feature (src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/journeys/linear/features/identification-numbers/): page.js (id and slug), evaluation.js (four scalar bindings), fields.js (four field names and the 58-character cap), controller.js (scope-filtered fields, Joi validation, recoverable save, next target), template.njk (govukInput per in-scope field, section caption, save actions), copy.en.js and copy.cy.js (title, labels, hints, error messages), identification-numbers.fit.spec.js (per commodity type branch: render and save, every validation rule, save-and-return and cancel, axe; plus two standalone tests). Consignment contact feature (features/consignment-contact-select/): page.js (slug consignment/contact/select), evaluation.js, fields.js (contactAddress), controller.js (search submit, blank save allowed, refusal of an id the book does not hold, commit of a copy of the record), template.njk (search box, inset of the selected address, results table with radios and View details disclosure, govukPagination, no-matches text, save actions), copy.en.js and copy.cy.js, view-model/index.js and view-model/pagination.js (binding the shared picker helpers to this page's slug and field), consignment-contact-select.fit.spec.js (render, reach from overview, first page and count, save controls, back link, search, no matches, selection kept through search and paging, saving, replacing, save-and-return, cancel, blank save for both submits, refusal and recovery, axe). Shared: journeys/linear/parties/index.js (dropping dangling address-book references on read), obligations/sections/parties.js (consignor, supplier, producer, crop and consignment number obligations) and obligations/sections/contact.js (contactAddress). The address-book-picker helpers (render.js, view-model.js, pagination.js, address-lines.js) were read for context only; part 6 claims their shared behaviour, and this part claims only what they make the contact page show. Hub status and row copy, the section caption copy and the address book PAGE_SIZE were looked up only to read the fit specs' assertions.

claims.statement: Treating a deleted address as if it were never entered is a recorded UCD decision.

A soft-deleted

claims.statement: Place of destination and consignor are stored as address book references and resolved from the book on every read, so a record the trader later corrects is corrected on the notification too.

A reference is an `{ addressId }` and nothing more: the details are resolved
 * from the book on every read, so a record the trader later corrects is

claims.statement: The consignment contact address is a copy, not a reference, so deleting the address book record it came from does not clear it from the notification.

`contactAddress` is that answer in

claims.statement: Dropping a dangling reference happens only for the current request; the stored answer is left until the next save rebuilds from the current answers, and the stored answers are kept so a page can tell 'answered, then deleted' from 'never answered'.
claims.quote:
Request-local. What was saved is left alone in the store — the next commit
 * that rebuilds from the current answers is what persists the clear — and the
 * engine keeps the stored answers beside the sanitised ones so a page can still
 * tell "answered, then deleted" from "never answered".

claims.statement: If the address book is unavailable while resolving a party reference, the error propagates rather than the reference being dropped as deleted.
